questions.question_english: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding the definitions under Section 2 of the RTE Act?
options_english: Child belonging to disadvantaged group — Only children belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
Elementary education — Education from class 1 to class 8
Capitation fee — Authorized fees collected by school management for infrastructure
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 2 of the Right to Education Act, 2009, 'elementary education' is defined as education from Class 1 to Class 8. The term 'child belonging to disadvantaged group' includes children from Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, socially and educationally backward classes, and other categories, not only SCs and STs. 'Capitation fee' means any donation or payment other than the fee notified by the school, and is prohibited. 'Local authority' refers to a Municipal Corporation, Municipal Council, Zila Parishad, Nagar Panchayat, or Panchayat, not the State Legislative Assembly. Therefore, only the pair in Option B is correctly matched.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (b) है। RTE अधिनियम, 2009 की धारा 2 के अनुसार 'प्रारंभिक शिक्षा' को कक्षा 1 से कक्षा 8 तक की शिक्षा के रूप में परिभाषित किया गया है। 'वंचित समूह से संबंधित बालक' में अनुसूचित जाति, अनुसूचित जनजाति, सामाजिक और शैक्षिक रूप से पिछड़े वर्ग और अन्य श्रेणियों के बच्चे शामिल हैं, न कि केवल SC और ST। 'कैपिटेशन शुल्क' का अर्थ विद्यालय द्वारा अधिसूचित शुल्क के अलावा कोई दान या भुगतान है, जो निषिद्ध है। 'स्थानीय प्राधिकरण' से तात्पर्य नगर निगम, नगर परिषद, जिला परिषद, नगर पंचायत या पंचायत से है, न कि राज्य विधान सभा से। अतः केवल विकल्प B सही ढंग से सुमेलित है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Elementary education — Education from class 1 to class 8
Section 2 defines elementary education as Class 1 to Class 8

questions.question_english: Which of the following statements correctly states the penalty for subjecting a child to a screening procedure for admission?
options_english: Fine up to Rs 10,000 for the first contravention and Rs 25,000 for each subsequent contravention.
Fine up to Rs 25,000 for the first contravention and Rs 50,000 for each subsequent contravention.
Fine up to Rs 50,000 for the first contravention and Rs 1,00,000 for each subsequent contravention.
Immediate withdrawal of school recognition on the first contravention.
questions.explanation_english: Section 13(2)(b) of the RTE Act, 2009 stipulates that any school or person subjecting a child to a screening procedure during admission shall be punishable with a fine up to twenty-five thousand rupees for the first contravention. Each subsequent contravention attracts a higher penalty of up to fifty thousand rupees. This graded penalty structure enforces compliance against discriminatory entry barriers without immediate withdrawal of recognition.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (b) है। RTE अधिनियम, 2009 की धारा 13(2)(ख) के अनुसार, यदि कोई स्कूल या व्यक्ति प्रवेश के दौरान किसी बच्चे को स्क्रीनिंग प्रक्रिया के अधीन करता है, तो पहले उल्लंघन के लिए पच्चीस हजार रुपये तक का मौद्रिक जुर्माना लगाया जा सकता है। प्रत्येक बाद के उल्लंघन के लिए यह जुर्माना पचास हजार रुपये तक बढ़ जाता है। यह प्रावधान प्रवेश के समय भेदभावपूर्ण बाधाओं के विरुद्ध अनुपालन सुनिश्चित करता है।
key_facts: Section 13(2)(b) prescribes penalty for screening procedure: fine up to Rs 25,000 for first contravention.
Each subsequent contravention attracts fine up to Rs 50,000.
No provision for immediate withdrawal of recognition on first contravention.
Printed answer key: (B) Fine up to Rs 25,000 for the first contravention and Rs 50,000 for each subsequent contravention.

questions.question_english: Under Section 26 of the RTE Act, the appointing authority shall ensure that the vacancy of teachers in a school under its control shall not exceed:
questions.explanation_english: Section 26 of the Right to Education Act, 2009 explicitly mandates that the appointing authority must ensure teaching vacancies in any school under its control do not exceed ten percent of the total sanctioned teacher strength. This statutory ceiling is designed to prevent chronic staffing shortages, guarantee uninterrupted classroom instruction, and uphold the mandated Pupil-Teacher Ratios across all elementary schools.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (b) है। आरटीई अधिनियम, 2009 की धारा 26 स्पष्ट रूप से यह आदेश देती है कि नियुक्ति प्राधिकारी को यह सुनिश्चित करना होगा कि उसके नियंत्रण में किसी भी विद्यालय में शिक्षण पदों की रिक्ति कुल स्वीकृत शिक्षक संख्या के दस प्रतिशत से अधिक न हो। यह वैधानिक सीमा पुरानी कर्मचारी कमी को रोकने, निर्बाध कक्षा शिक्षण सुनिश्चित करने और सभी प्राथमिक विद्यालयों में अनिवार्य छात्र-शिक्षक अनुपात को बनाए रखने के लिए डिज़ाइन की गई है।
key_facts: Section 26 of RTE Act 2009 caps teacher vacancies at 10% of sanctioned strength
Aims to prevent chronic staffing shortages and maintain PTR norms
Printed answer key: (B) 10% of the total sanctioned strength

माता-पिता को आधिकारिक लिखित चेतावनी जारी करना कि वे स्कूल के आंतरिक शैक्षणिक मामलों में हस्तक्षेप न करें।

questions.question_english: A teacher in an upper primary school physically strikes a student for failing to complete homework. The parents complain to the Principal. Under Section 17 of the RTE Act, what is the mandatory course of action for the Principal?
options_english: Initiate disciplinary action against the teacher under service rules.
Counsel the student in private to maintain strict discipline and ensure timely completion of assigned daily homework.
Immediately transfer the affected student to another classroom section to avoid further interpersonal conflict.
Issue an official written warning to the parents advising them against interfering in internal school academic matters.
questions.explanation_english: Section 17 of the RTE Act explicitly prohibits physical punishment and mental harassment in schools. When a teacher inflicts physical punishment, the Principal is legally obligated to initiate disciplinary proceedings against the teacher under the applicable service rules. The other options—counselling the student, transferring the student, or warning the parents—are contrary to the spirit of the Act, which places the onus on the school to protect the child and hold the teacher accountable. The Act mandates a zero-tolerance policy towards corporal punishment.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (a) है। RTE अधिनियम की धारा 17 स्कूलों में शारीरिक दंड और मानसिक उत्पीड़न को स्पष्ट रूप से प्रतिबंधित करती है। जब कोई शिक्षक शारीरिक दंड देता है, तो प्रधानाचार्य कानूनी रूप से लागू सेवा नियमों के तहत शिक्षक के विरुद्ध अनुशासनात्मक कार्यवाही शुरू करने के लिए बाध्य होता है। अन्य विकल्प—छात्र को परामर्श देना, छात्र को स्थानांतरित करना, या माता-पिता को चेतावनी देना—अधिनियम की भावना के विपरीत हैं, जो बच्चे की रक्षा और शिक्षक को जवाबदेह ठहराने की जिम्मेदारी स्कूल पर डालता है। अधिनियम शारीरिक दंड के प्रति शून्य-सहनशीलता की नीति अनिवार्य करता है।
key_facts: Section 17 prohibits physical punishment and mental harassment.
Principal must initiate disciplinary action against the teacher under service rules.
Zero-tolerance policy for corporal punishment in schools.
Printed answer key: (A) Initiate disciplinary action against the teacher under service rules.

II. बच्चे को रोकना (यदि राज्य नीति अनुमति देती है)
III. पुनर्परीक्षा का अवसर

questions.question_english:
Arrange the correct sequence of actions for a student failing the Class 5 regular examination under the amended RTE Act:
I. Declaration of regular exam result
II. Holding back the child (if State policy permits)
III. Opportunity for re-examination
IV. Additional instruction/remedial classes
questions.explanation_english: The statutory procedure following regular Class 5 examinations requires first declaring the annual exam results. If a student fails, the institution must provide additional remedial instruction, followed by conducting a re-examination within two months. Only if the student fails this re-examination can detention be enforced, provided the appropriate State Government has formally notified such a holding-back policy. This sequence is mandated by the amended Section 16 of the RTE Act.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (a) है। संशोधित RTE अधिनियम की धारा 16 के अनुसार, कक्षा 5 की नियमित परीक्षा के बाद सबसे पहले वार्षिक परीक्षा परिणाम घोषित किया जाता है। यदि छात्र अनुत्तीर्ण होता है, तो संस्था को अतिरिक्त उपचारात्मक निर्देश प्रदान करना होता है, जिसके बाद दो महीने के भीतर पुनर्परीक्षा आयोजित की जाती है। केवल यदि छात्र इस पुनर्परीक्षा में भी अनुत्तीर्ण होता है, तो उसे रोका जा सकता है, बशर्ते राज्य सरकार ने ऐसी रोक नीति को अधिसूचित किया हो। यह क्रम संशोधित अधिनियम द्वारा अनिवार्य है।
key_facts: The amended RTE Act (Section 16) prescribes a specific sequence for detention after Class 5/8 exams.
First step: Declaration of regular exam result.
Second step: Additional instruction/remedial classes for failed students.
Third step: Re-examination within two months.
Fourth step: Holding back only if re-examination failed and State policy permits.
Printed answer key: (A) I, IV, III, II

questions.question_english: According to Section 21 of the RTE Act, which category of schools is exempted from the mandatory constitution of a School Management Committee (SMC)?
options_english: Unaided private schools receiving no government grants.
Government-aided schools receiving partial financial grants from the state
Schools established, owned, or directly controlled by the appropriate Government
Unrecognized private institutions operating without state accreditation
questions.explanation_english: Section 21 of the RTE Act mandates the constitution of School Management Committees (SMCs) in government, government-aided, and specified category schools. Unaided private schools that receive no financial aid from the state are explicitly exempted from this mandatory SMC requirement. However, such schools remain subject to state-specific rules governing parent-teacher associations or advisory management bodies. This exemption recognizes the autonomy of purely private unaided institutions while ensuring accountability in publicly funded schools.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (a) है। आरटीई अधिनियम की धारा 21 सरकारी, सरकारी सहायता प्राप्त और निर्दिष्ट श्रेणी के विद्यालयों में विद्यालय प्रबंधन समितियों (एसएमसी) के गठन को अनिवार्य बनाती है। सरकार से कोई वित्तीय सहायता प्राप्त न करने वाले निजी गैर-सहायता प्राप्त विद्यालयों को इस अनिवार्य एसएमसी आवश्यकता से स्पष्ट रूप से छूट दी गई है। हालांकि, ऐसे विद्यालय अभिभावक-शिक्षक संघों या सलाहकार प्रबंधन निकायों को नियंत्रित करने वाले राज्य-विशिष्ट नियमों के अधीन रहते हैं। यह छूट पूरी तरह से निजी गैर-सहायता प्राप्त संस्थानों की स्वायत्तता को मान्यता देती है जबकि सार्वजनिक रूप से वित्त पोषित विद्यालयों में जवाबदेही सुनिश्चित करती है।
key_facts: Statutory basis: Section 21 of the RTE Act, 2009

questions.question_english:
Read the following assertion (A) and reason (R) statements and select the correct option:
Assertion (A): The Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) prescribed by the RTE Act is lower for primary schools compared to upper primary schools.
Reason (R): Younger children in primary classes require more individual attention and closer pedagogical support.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.explanation_english: The RTE Act Schedule prescribes a Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) of 30:1 for primary classes (Classes 1-5) and 35:1 for upper primary classes (Classes 6-8). A lower numerical ratio (30:1) indicates fewer pupils per teacher at the primary level, making Assertion (A) true. However, Reason (R) is false because the prescribed PTR norms are statutory standards based on infrastructure and teacher availability; the Act does not explicitly link the lower primary PTR to the pedagogical needs of younger children, and the reason misstates the basis of the numerical comparison. Therefore, A is true but R is false.

questions.question_english: The rationale behind moving away from the strict "no-detention" policy to a discretionary "holding back" policy in 2019 was primarily due to:

questions.explanation_english: The 2019 amendment to the RTE Act replaced the absolute no-detention policy with a discretionary holding-back provision because evidence from national surveys (such as ASER) showed declining learning outcomes. Automatic promotion without remedial assessment led to students reaching higher grades without foundational literacy and numeracy, reducing academic accountability among teachers and students. The change aimed to restore learning standards while allowing states to design context-specific remedial measures.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (b) है। 2019 में आरटीई अधिनियम में संशोधन ने पूर्ण नो-डिटेंशन नीति को विवेकाधीन रोक-रखने के प्रावधान से बदल दिया क्योंकि राष्ट्रीय सर्वेक्षणों (जैसे ASER) के प्रमाणों ने सीखने के परिणामों में गिरावट दिखाई। उपचारात्मक मूल्यांकन के बिना स्वत: पदोन्नति के कारण छात्र बुनियादी साक्षरता और संख्यात्मकता के बिना उच्च कक्षाओं में पहुंच गए, जिससे शिक्षकों और छात्रों में शैक्षणिक जवाबदेही कम हुई। इस परिवर्तन का उद्देश्य राज्यों को संदर्भ-विशिष्ट उपचारात्मक उपाय डिजाइन करने की अनुमति देते हुए सीखने के मानकों को बहाल करना था।

questions.question_english: Who is empowered under Article 350A to issue such directions to any State as considered necessary or proper for securing the provision of facilities for instruction in the mother-tongue?
questions.explanation_english: Article 350A of the Constitution of India mandates that every State and local authority shall endeavour to provide adequate facilities for instruction in the mother-tongue at the primary stage to children belonging to linguistic minority groups. Crucially, it empowers the President of India to issue directions to any State as considered necessary or proper for securing the provision of such facilities. questions.explanation_english: Section 13(1) of the RTE Act, 2009 explicitly prohibits capitation fees and any screening procedure during admission. Therefore, only statements I, II and III are prohibited.
